p: two of whom were married to two sisters and one who was married to an unrelated woman,
The husband of one of the sisters died
who was married to the unrelated woman married,
the sister of one’s wife, … and the second … due to … rival wife.
the sister of one’s wife, as she is the sister of this brother’s wife, and the second woman is dismissed due to her status as the first woman’s rival wife.
perform ḥalitza and may not enter into levirate marriage.
The reason that the mishna requires ḥalitza is specifically because he,
had he not performed levirate betrothal with her,
enter into levirate marriage as well.
two of whom were married to two sisters and one who was married to an unrelated woman,
He who was married to the unrelated woman died,
and one of the husbands of the sisters married his wife, … and … died … The first … is dismissed … due to … the sister of his wife.

and one of the husbands of the sisters married his wife, and then died childless as well. The first woman, i.e., the sister who was originally married to the brother who performed levirate marriage, is dismissed and is exempt from levirate marriage due to her status as the sister of his wife.
perform ḥalitza and may not enter into levirate marriage,

p: it was beloved to him and he taught it earlier. … However,

it was beloved to him and he taught it earlier. In truth, it would have now been possible to eliminate the present mishna, for there was no longer any novelty in it; its ruling could be derived by an a fortiori argument from the previous ruling. However,
a mishna does not move from its place.
g: ומתוך שהיא חביבה לו, משום שיש בה חידוש, הקדים אותה

p: two of whom were married to two sisters and one who was married to an unrelated woman,
One of the husbands of the sisters died,
and he who was married to the unrelated woman married
the wife of the second … died.
the wife of the second brother, the other one of the sisters, died.
who was married to the unrelated woman died,
forbidden to him at one time,
Any yevama to whom the verse “Her brother-in-law will have intercourse with her” … cannot be applied at the time that she happens
Any yevama to whom the verse “Her brother-in-law will have intercourse with her” (Deuteronomy 25:5) cannot be applied at the time that she happens
like the wife of a brother
She is forbidden to him forever,
since she was forbidden to him at one time.

p: lest you say that this … applies
two brothers who were married to two sisters,
died and afterward the wife of the second … died, … then she,
died and afterward the wife of the second brother died, then she,
since she was forbidden to him

this household completely, i.e., from the entire obligation of levirate marriage. She received total exemption from the mitzva of levirate marriage because this obligation applied only to the one remaining brother, and she was forbidden to him at the time that she happened before him for levirate marriage. But here,
where she was not completely precluded from … this household
where she was not completely precluded from entering this household
who was married to the unrelated woman,
she is eligible for this … as well,
she is eligible for this second brother following the death of his wife as well,
two of whom were married to two sisters and one who was married to an unrelated woman,
the husband of one of the sisters,
who was married to the unrelated woman, … died, … and … the man who divorced … married, … her, … And
who was married to the unrelated woman, died, and Shimon, the man who divorced his wife, married, i.e., performed levirate marriage with, her, i.e., this unrelated woman. And
And according to Rav Ashi, … Rav Naḥman … difficult, … Rav Ashi … said to you:

And according to Rav Ashi, that which Rav Naḥman said is difficult, as Rav Naḥman deduced from the earlier mishna that the levirate bond is not substantial even in the case of a single brother. The Gemara answers: Rav Ashi could have said to you:
the same is true even … where he
the same is true even in the case where he
did not perform levirate betrothal with her.
the unrelated woman must perform ḥalitza and may not enter into levirate marriage
